ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Gibraltar primary law: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 1-8 (incorporation), ss. 9-12 (registered office), Part 9 and Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2018 (confidential UBO register); Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar); Criminal Justice (Money Laundering) Regulations 2019 (Gibraltar), regs. 7-10, 13-18 (customer due diligence); Financial Services Act 2019 and Financial Services Commission Act 2005 (AML/CFT supervision by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission); Sanctions Act 2019 (UN/EU sanctions implementation). Shareholder-piercing law: Bermuda Companies Act 1981, ss. 74 and 87-92A (beneficial ownership records, exemption certificate and non-resident ownership); Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 (Bermuda); Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing (AML/ATF) Code of Practice 2024 (Bermuda). The contemplated structure is intended to be tax-exempt in Bermuda (no corporate income tax on exempted companies) and, in Gibraltar, to qualify as a non-resident company with nil Gibraltar income tax on foreign-sourced distribution income under the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar) as amended.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (Gibraltar registrant vehicle: UBO register accessible to the Registrar of Companies, GFSC, law enforcement and regulated entities performing CDD with consent, not publicly searchable); Private_Internal (Bermuda shareholder level: confidential beneficial ownership register maintained by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies without public access)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, officer, and authorized signatory against the HM Treasury UK Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU sanctions as retained by Gibraltar, and Gibraltar's domestic Sanctions Act 2019 annexes. Continuous PEP flags are applied via licensed automated AML/CFT screening software with a minimum matching threshold of 98%, followed by case-based disposition and negative news review. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP status, adverse media, sanctions proximity, or any single Swift TT / wire transfer at or above USD 10,000, and the screening output must be refreshed no less frequently than every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry e-Services portal (https://www.gibraltarcompaniesregistry.gi) operated by the Office of the Registrar of Companies, Government of Gibraltar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the statutory language. All company names must be expressed in the Latin/Roman alphabet using standard letters, Arabic numerals and limited permitted punctuation (full stop, ampersand, comma, apostrophe, hyphen). Foreign-script trading names must be transliterated into Roman characters and, where the applicant also submits a translation, the Gibraltar Registrar may require a statutory declaration confirming that the transliterated or translated form corresponds to the original foreign name. Extended diacritical glyphs and non-Latin scripts are not accepted in the registered corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No administrative extension of the 30-day reservation is available; a lapsed reservation requires a fresh application and fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may within 14 calendar days file a written notice of objection with the Registrar of Companies together with the standard name clearance application form, a copy of the refusal notice, and a reasoned submission citing Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar) section 8(3). The Registrar must issue a written determination within 28 days. Further challenge lies by originating motion to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under Order 53 of the Rules of the Supreme Court within 42 days of the final refusal. Sensitive-word consents must be obtained in advance from the responsible minister or regulator (e.g., Financial Services Commission for 'Bank', 'Insurance', 'Trust').

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted. The Gibraltar vehicle must maintain a physical registered office in Gibraltar, which may be supplied by a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider as a professional registered-office address without the company leasing separate floor space. A virtual/agency office is permissible for this ISIC 4631 wholesale distribution activity because cross-border procurement and distribution of organic matcha powder is not a geographically mobile high-risk activity and does not of itself create a Gibraltar taxable presence, provided the licensed agent retains custody of statutory records and the company satisfies the applicable non-resident tax status test under the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar) if it commences local trading or hiring.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspection by the Registrar or the GFSC in the first 12 months is below 3% for a low-risk, agent-administered distribution vehicle with no local employees. The probability rises to approximately 60-70% if the company records first-year turnover above USD 5,000,000 without corresponding local substance, if any OFAC/UN/EU sanctions hit or PEP anomaly is flagged, or if the banking institution initiates a compliance review under its financial crime monitoring program.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981 (as amended), in particular sections 14 (exempted company classification), 1-4 (mode of incorporation and memorandum), 18-19 (registration), 135 (registered office), and 274 (resident representative); read together with the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 for issuance of the tax-exempt status certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Registry, Ministry of Finance (Bermuda); filings accepted through licensed corporate service providers in Hamilton, Bermuda.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration of the Memorandum of Association, submitted together with Form CO/EX (Application for Registration of an Exempted Company) and accompanying statutory declarations.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Companies Act 1981 for exempted companies; a founding subscriber must subscribe for at least one fully paid share of par value (commonly USD 1.00), and no escrow account, capital deposit, or capital duty is required. Authorised capital of USD 12,000 is recommended to optimise the annual government fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws of the Company, as filed with the Registrar of Companies in Bermuda, are adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Company allot and issue one fully paid ordinary share of USD 1.00 to the founding subscriber for subsequent transfer to the beneficial owner in Schedule A. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office be established at the licensed registered office provider in Bermuda, who shall act as resident representative. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] and [Name] be appointed first directors, and [Name] Corporate Secretary, with authority to execute banking documents and open accounts. RESOLVED FURTHER that the common seal be adopted and this resolution entered in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Availability Pre-Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Ministry of Finance (Bermuda) — online name search facility, or licensed corporate service provider submitting a Form CO/NC name clearance request.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search against the Bermuda register and file a name clearance application through a licensed corporate service provider. Confirm that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing or protected name and does not contain restricted terms such as 'Bank', 'Trust', or 'Insurance' without a sector licence.
required_dossiers: Name clearance request (Form CO/NC)
Copy of subscriber passport and proof of residential address
CSP engagement letter confirming incorporation purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or reserved for another entity, the CSP submits up to three alternative names within 24 hours; no additional government fee is payable for a substitution made before incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed corporate service provider or Bermuda-licensed law firm acting as the applicant for the Registrar of Companies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association (name, capital clause, exempted company declaration, object powers) and Bye-Laws; prepare the founder's written consent. Have the subscriber and proposed directors execute before a notary public or British consul, and where the executing party is outside the United Kingdom, obtain an apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention 1961.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association
Draft Bye-Laws
Written consent of founding subscriber
Notarised subscriber and director declarations
Banking AML/KYC questionnaire and beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registrar queries concerning restrictive or ultra vires clauses are cured by amending the memorandum through a supplemental subscriber resolution and refiling before fee settlement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Incorporation Application to the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies (Bermuda), Ministry of Finance Building, Hamilton, via the Bermuda Companies e-Services portal or through the licensed CSP's authorised submission account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Memorandum and Bye-Laws together with Form CO/EX, the name clearance certificate, the section 18 statutory declarations, and the consent of the registered office provider and resident representative. Pay the application fee by wire transfer using the exact fee code supplied by the Registrar; retain the portal receipt as conclusive filing evidence.
required_dossiers: Form CO/EX (Application for Registration of an Exempted Company)
Executed Memorandum of Association
Executed Bye-Laws
Name clearance certificate
Statutory declarations of subscriber and first directors
Form CO/RO consent of registered office provider and resident representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or supplementary-evidence request, the CSP must respond within 21 calendar days; defective declarations are corrected by a fresh electronic notarised declaration filed before expiry of the requisition period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies in conjunction with the Accountant General (Bermuda); fee collection through the CSP's settlement account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the incorporation fee of USD 1,780 together with the first year's exempted company annual fee. Upon clearance, the Registrar stamps the memorandum, allocates the company number, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the exact legal name, company number, and date of incorporation and enter them in the company's statutory records.
required_dossiers: Fee remittance confirmation and fee code reference
Certificate of Incorporation (official instrument issued)
Company number allocation notice
Registrar receipt of stamped memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A late or incorrectly coded payment triggers a 10% default penalty; cure by expedited wire with the correct fee code and, where the certificate is misstated, request a rectification certificate under the Companies Act rectification arrangements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Formalities and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Secretary (Bermuda) and the licensed registered office provider in Hamilton, Bermuda.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution adopting the constitutional documents, issuing the founders' share certificate, appointing directors, the Corporate Secretary and the resident representative, and adopting the common seal. File the registered office confirmation and open the company registers (members, directors, officers, charges, and beneficial ownership registers). Confirm that the exempted status certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 has been issued.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written consent of the first board meeting
Share certificate of the founding subscriber
Form CO/RO registered office confirmation with provider consent
Statutory registers of members, directors and officers
Exempted status certificate issued by the Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar flags a deficiency in the registered office designation, an amended Form CO/RO with the provider's fresh consent is refiled; a change of registered office takes effect within five working days and is publicised in the register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar Trade Bridge and Administrative Utility Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission for any Gibraltar letterbox or administrative office; UK Companies House only where an interposed UK branch is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Bermuda exempted company as a foreign company branch in Gibraltar under the Gibraltar Companies (Foreign Companies) Act, or alternatively rely solely on the Bermuda corporate domicile and the Gibraltar EMI banking rail in Stage 3. For pure cross-border matcha wholesale distribution no operating subsidiary is required; execute a simple physical address agreement and notify the Gibraltar business registration office of the trade activity.
required_dossiers: Certified and apostilled Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copies of Memorandum and Bye-Laws
Apostilled register of directors and officers
Gibraltar foreign company branch application form (where applicable)
Registered office service agreement for the Gibraltar administrative address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apostille or legalisation deficiencies are cured by re-certifying the submission bundle at the Bermuda Governor's office or the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office Legalisation Office; branch registration refusals are corrected by amending the address details and refiling within seven working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bermuda Revenue Authority — Trade and Business Licensing Department (for the Bermuda Trade & Business License); HM Government of Gibraltar Trade and Business Licensing Office for any Gibraltar-fronted operating address. No industrial manufacturing board applies to ISIC 4631 wholesale distribution of packaged matcha powder.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Trade & Business License (Wholesale/Distribution class) under the Trade & Business Licensing Act 1993 (Bermuda); supplementary Food Business Operator Registration under applicable food hygiene rules (Gibraltar Food Safety Act 2014 and Regulation (EC) 852/2004) where storage or transshipment physically occurs.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (Bermuda); Gibraltar Environmental Safety and Health Agency for any Gibraltar transit warehouse footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 3 (Low Impact Storage and Distribution): no Environmental Impact Statement or Registration required because the activity consists solely of warehousing and wholesale distribution of hermetically sealed organic matcha powder with no manufacturing, combustion, or process discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater discharge; compliance with WHO Guidelines for Drinking-Water Quality for any wash-down stations; storage temperature maintained at or below 5°C for ceremonial-grade matcha; fugitive dust and VOC emissions from packaging areas limited to below 0.5 tonnes VOC per annum; waste handling per the Waste Framework Directive (2008/98/EC) and the Bermuda Clean Air Act 1991 where any incineration is used.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service or Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service, covering extinguisher inspection, fire doors, evacuation plans, and smoke detection for the covered warehouse; structural load inspection certificate for racked storage above 2.4 metres signed by an EU/UK-accredited structural engineer; occupational clearance under the Bermuda Occupational Health and Safety Act 2003 and the UK Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 confirming matcha dust exposure below the occupational exposure limit of 1 mg/m³ (inhalable fraction), with HEPA vacuuming, sanitary changing facilities, and forklift operator certifications maintained on site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office (ITO), H.M. Government of Gibraltar, Ministry of Finance - online portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax-office; parallel goods-clearance authority: Gibraltar Customs & Excise Department, port and common transit (NCTS) filings via the Gibraltar single window (BASS/ACTIVE declarations).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company (BM_EXEMPTED_CO) establishing a branch or place of business in Gibraltar must: (1) register as a 'foreign company' with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014 (Part XXIII) within one month of establishment, filing certified constitutional documents, register of directors/secretary, local registered-office agreement and proof of a local Process Agent, obtaining a Gibraltar FC-company reference number; (2) file a Notification of Liability to Tax (Form NLT) with the Income Tax Office within 30 days of commencing the Gibraltarian business activity, using the FC reference to obtain a Gibraltar Identification Number (GIN/Tax Reference) from ITO; (3) if claiming territorial exemption on foreign-source matcha-trade income, apply for the foreign-source income exemption at ITO with board resolutions, substance documentation (physical office, local secretary, management minutes in Gibraltar) and a forecast of non-Gibraltar revenue; (4) register as a customs declarant/importer with the Gibraltar Customs & Excise Department and appoint a licensed customs agent where goods will physically transit or be warehoused in Gibraltar. No minimum capital is required for the branch; annual returns, tax-return filing and GDP (gross domestic profit) computations are due on the normal 30 September and 31 January deadlines.

stage_3.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope / Tax_Exempt_Zone. The Bermuda Exempted Company is, in its home jurisdiction, tax-exempt under Bermuda's Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 (exemption from future Bermuda income tax until 2035) and is not a pass-through: it is a limited-liability body corporate. In Gibraltar, the branch is brought within the territorial corporate-tax system under the Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended): tax is chargeable at 12.5% only on income arising in or derived from Gibraltar, while profits derived solely from foreign procurement and offshore resale of matcha powder, together with foreign-source dividends, interest and capital gains, are outside the Gibraltarian charge (0% effective rate on such income, provided substance requirements are satisfied and no Gibraltarian PE/activity gives rise to local-source trading).
stage_3.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) Territorial-basis election for foreign-source income exclusion under the Income Tax Act 2010 territorial provisions (default for non-resident companies, with election/commitment required for companies treated as resident); (2) Application for a Certificate/Confirmation of Foreign Source Income Exemption (qualifying-conditions route) proving economic substance and administrative control in Gibraltar; (3) Group relief election under the Income Tax Act for surrender of losses among Gibraltarian group members; (4) Capital-allowances pooling election on any Gibraltarian fixed assets; (5) Hybrid-mismatch notification regime: no US-style check-the-box election exists under Gibraltarian law, but taxpayers must apply the OECD/G20 BEPS Action 2 hybrid-mismatch rules and may elect structural alignment (Governing-Entity treatment) to ensure the Bermuda parent and Gibraltar branch are not recharacterised; all elections are filed through the ITO online portal and are irrevocable without Commissioner consent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar (Currency Notes Act 1934) is the issuing authority for the Gibraltar Pound (GIP), pegged at 1:1 to GBP; regulatory supervision of banking and payment institutions is exercised by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC); the Bank of England provides the underlying GBP backing. Bermuda imposes no central bank exchange-control mandate over exempted companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility. GIP is legally pegged to GBP, eliminating intra-GIP convertibility risk. No exchange-control legislation exists in either Gibraltar or Bermuda; no statutory restrictions apply to dividend distribution, loan repayment, capital repatriation, or profit remittance, and no withholding taxes are levied by either jurisdiction. Trading proceeds in USD and JPY are freely convertible into GIP/GBP or may be retained in multicurrency accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Gibraltar and Bermuda impose no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. A Bermuda Exempted Company may hold export receivables indefinitely in any freely convertible currency without GFSC or Bermuda Monetary Authority conversion obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account with trade finance and LC desk
Capital Escrow Account / Wealth Management Vault

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-TO-MEDIUM. GFSC-licensed Electronic Money Institutions are few and typically require Gibraltar substance through a regulated fiduciary; post-Brexit, UK and EU EMI passporting no longer covers Gibraltar. Most UK FCA-authorised EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Currencycloud) will decline a Bermuda Exempted Company with non-resident nominee directors under UK Money Laundering Regulations 2017 unless the entity is introduced by an approved Gibraltar TCSP and maintains a Gibraltar-resident signatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted in principle under the GFSC AML Guidance Notes through video-identification and certified digital documents, but Tier-1 Gibraltar banks uniformly require at least one beneficial owner or statutory director to complete an in-person or notarially-witnessed interview (physically in Gibraltar or before a recognized notary in a correspondent jurisdiction). Pure remote onboarding without a local introducer is not practically available for a Bermuda Exempted Company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore exempted company with no physical or economic footprint in Bermuda or Gibraltar
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Exemption; Bermuda Register of Members and Register of Directors; Beneficial Ownership (BOR) filing receipt from Bermuda Registrar of Companies; group structure chart; economic substance declaration under Bermuda's Economic Substance Act 2018 (or documented Gibraltar tax-residence rationale); introduction letter from a licensed Gibraltar TCSP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholder or omnibus trust controlling the exempted company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory declaration of beneficial ownership; certified trust deed or nominee agreement; source-of-wealth dossier for each natural person with 25%+ control; undertaking to file any beneficial-ownership change within 30 days; audited or management accounts evidencing commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party funding or rapid inbound capital injection without trade nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed bank reference from the remitting institution; share subscription resolution of the board; proof of funding source (sale of prior business, legal dividend, or disposal of assets); executed purchase agreements with matcha suppliers to demonstrate intended commercial utilisation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade counterparties domiciled in Japan/China, triggering enhanced due diligence on origin of goods and payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices and purchase contracts between the Exempted Company, Japanese tea co-operatives, and Chinese exporters; Bill of Lading and air waybill history; phytosanitary certificates and organic certification; supplier KYC profiles obtained through a reputable corporate data utility (e.g., Dun & Bradstreet); written declaration that no sanctioned goods, dual-use items, or restricted agricultural tariffs apply.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 wire to the Gibraltar bank account, referencing 'Share Capital Subscription' and including the corporate resolution date in field 70 (Remittance Information). The remitting bank must be a regulated financial institution with a clear KYC file; Gibraltar banks will require a source-of-wealth questionnaire for any single injection above USD 50,000 and will verify the corporate authorisation via the provisioned board resolution, certificate of incumbency, and register of members. Recommended to route through a prime London or Hong Kong correspondent to avoid intermediary sanctions screening delays; use the Gibraltar account IBAN and include UETR (Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference) with every wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'TRADE_GOODS' for open-account telegraphic transfers in JPY, USD, or EUR to approved matcha suppliers; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) issued under UCP600 for Japanese tea-cooperative purchases, documentary collection (MT400/MT900) as a cost-attenuating alternative; (3) SWIFT MT760 standby L/C where suppliers request performance security. Each disbursement must be accompanied by commercial invoice, packing list, Bill of Lading, and organic certificate to satisfy both the bank's trade surveillance and UK/Gibraltar sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (GBP/GIP vs USD and JPY) with maturities up to 12 months for matcha procurement budgeting
FX swaps (USD/JPY and GBP/JPY) to cover working-capital gaps between supplier payables and buyer receivables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing CNY/CNH only, where onshore Chinese settlement is restricted; no NDF required for JPY as JPY is fully convertible
Cross-currency swaps (USD/GBP and JPY/GBP) for matched medium-term trade-debt structuring
OTC vanilla European FX options to cap matcha-cost volatility without limiting upside on USD-denominated sales

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempted Company Annual Return and Government Fee (Bermuda)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation; fee due in two installments (31 January and 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of USD 200 per month or 10% of annual fee; strike-off proceedings after 12 months in arrears; directors subject to personal liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of GBP 50 per day up to GBP 1,500; administrative strike-off after 3 months of non-compliance under Section 294 of the Gibraltar Companies Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Beneficial Ownership Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to GBP 5,000 and daily default fine of GBP 500; director disqualification for persistent breach

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Gibraltar: audit required if a company exceeds two of three thresholds – turnover > GBP 10.2m, total assets > GBP 5.1m, employees > 50. Bermuda: audit mandatory if gross assets exceed USD 10m or annual revenue exceeds USD 25m; otherwise audit may be waived by shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Gibraltar: UK-adopted International Financial Reporting Standards (UK-IFRS) or Financial Reporting Standard 102 (FRS 102). Bermuda: IFRS or US GAAP, with Bermuda compliant GAAP for regulated entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Gibraltar: annual UBO-1 confirmation filed with the Registrar, certifying the accuracy of beneficial ownership data and reflecting any shareholding transfers; updates required within 14 days of a change. Bermuda: no public UBO filing, but annual Certificate of Compliance and confidential economic substance declaration required; share transfers must be recorded in the company's register and reported to the local corporate service provider.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 6% rate on the first GIP 350,000 of taxable profits for qualifying small and medium-sized companies; territorial basis of taxation excludes foreign-source trading income neither arising in nor remitted to Gibraltar; no capital gains tax and no VAT/GST on matcha powder trade.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Corporate Income Tax Return (Form CT-1) — filed electronically via the Income Tax Office (ITO) e-Filing portal (GRX / Taxes & Duties Online).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed no later than 30 November following the end of the year of assessment in which the accounting period ends; for a 31 December year-end the filing and final payment deadline is 30 November of the following calendar year. Non-calendar-year accounting periods: due date is the following 30 November unless the accounting period ends after 30 September, in which case an extension to the next 30 November may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Gibraltar registration number, ITO tax reference, registered office address, date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident shareholders and directors; state the 'Bermuda Exempted Company' structural status and the jurisdiction of tax residence (Bermuda or Gibraltar).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the chargeable accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: First return may cover up to 18 months from incorporation; quarterly instalment scheme entries to be completed for large companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross worldwide receipts from wholesale and distribution of organic matcha powder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source trading income (negotiated and delivered outside Gibraltar, proceeds retained abroad) should be disclosed here and then excluded under the territorial rule; retain contracts, invoices and payment channel records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Cost of Sales & Operating Expenditure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Procurement costs, freight, warehousing, salaries, marketing and professional fees attributable to the matcha trade.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party purchases from Japanese/Bermuda affiliates must be benchmarked at arm's length and referenced to the TP disclosure in Box 6; cross-border payment evidence to be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted for non-deductible items and capital allowances (depreciation add-back, losses disallowed).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must limit the computation to income attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment; supporting asset/expenditure apportionment schedules required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of all controlled transactions: parties, nature, consideration, transfer pricing method applied and mark-up.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the Local File summary if aggregate controlled transactions exceed GIP 1,000,000; attach Form TP-1 (transactions schedule) and the Master File if group turnover exceeds GIP 50,000,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trading losses from prior periods set off against current profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset restricted to same trade and subject to a 5-year carry-forward limit and continuity of ownership test; indicate the loss origin year and amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chargeable income multiplied by 12.5% (6% for the small-companies band); foreign tax credits and DTA relief claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Certificate of Tax Residence for treaty claims and compute the UK/Gibraltar DTA (2020) relief on any Gibraltar-source interest or royalty income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of core income-generating activities (CIGA), employees, premises and board meeting locations in Gibraltar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bermuda-exempt-style companies must evidence management and control in Gibraltar; cross-reference the ESR filing and retain board minutes, employment records and lease agreements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of GIP 100, increasing to GIP 1,000 after three months, plus daily surcharge of GIP 60 (maximum GIP 3,600); negligent or fraudulent returns: penalty up to 100% of the tax understated; criminal liability for deliberate evasion with fines of up to GIP 500,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on dividends paid by a Gibraltar company to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since no Gibraltar dividend withholding tax is exigible, the UK-resident shareholder obtains a Gibraltar Certificate of Tax Residence from the Commissioner of Income Tax and submits it to HMRC to support any foreign tax credit claim for underlying Gibraltar corporate tax; beneficial ownership documentation (share register, board minutes declaring the dividend) must be retained. For payments to shareholders resident in other DTA jurisdictions, submit the relevant Treaty Relief Declaration (Form G-DTA) to the ITO before effecting payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law: 0% withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Under the UK–Gibraltar DTA (2020), qualifying interest and royalty payments also attract a 0% rate, subject to beneficial ownership and the submission of the UK-resident recipient's HMRC-residence certificate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where aggregate controlled transactions exceed GIP 1,000,000 per annum; Master File: mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds GIP 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report follows the OECD threshold of EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations 2019 (Schedule 2 of the Income Tax Act 2010) classify 'distribution and service business' as a relevant activity; the matcha trading company must maintain (i) board meetings and strategic direction in Gibraltar, (ii) adequate physical premises and employees, and (iii) performance of core income-generating activities in Gibraltar. The Bermuda Exempted Company classification does not eliminate ESR duties: if control and management are found to be in Bermuda, the entity falls under Bermuda's Economic Substance Act 2018, requiring equivalent CIGA presence in Bermuda and annual ESR reporting to the Registrar.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of matcha powder sales receipts from the Gibraltar CT-1 return, fabrication of procurement invoices, or mischaracterization of Gibraltar-source income as territorial/foreign-source income to exploit the 0% effective rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 100% of the tax evaded plus statutory interest; criminal fines up to GIP 500,000; confiscation of the proceeds of the matcha trade under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and executive directors who sign false returns are personally liable for civil restitution of the evaded tax; courts may impose travel bans, exclusion from directorships for up to 15 years, and imprisonment of up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Bermuda Exempted-style company as a letterbox entity with no employees, no board meetings in Gibraltar, and no core income-generating activities while routing matcha procurement and distribution payments through Gibraltar to obtain the territorial exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure of the ESR test: penalty of GIP 10,000 rising to GIP 1,000 per day (capped at GIP 50,000) and automatic exchange of information with HMRC and Bermuda; the company may be struck off the Gibraltar register and lose tax-residence status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to exercise real management and control are jointly and severally assessed for the company's unpaid tax on piercing of the corporate veil; disqualification orders under the Companies Act 2014 and liability for ESR penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Shifting profits to a related Japanese matcha supplier or a Bermuda affiliate by setting non-arm's-length purchase prices, excessive management fees, or unrealistic procurement mark-ups without TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable profits at 12.5% with statutory interest; penalty up to 100% of the tax shortfall for failure to maintain the Local File/Master File; CbC-related penalties for non-filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the intercompany pricing and failed to commission an OECD-compliant benchmarking study are jointly and severally liable for the tax adjustment and face director disqualification proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unlicensed payment aggregators or non-bank EMIs in the United Kingdom to convert matcha trade receivables without customer due diligence, or structuring payments to avoid the AML reporting obligations of the Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines of up to GIP 1,000,000; confiscation orders over trade proceeds; revocation of the company's exempted status and banking facilities; regulatory censure by the GFSC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual liability: imprisonment of up to 14 years for money-laundering; travel bans and asset-freezing orders; personal confiscation orders and permanent disqualification from acting as a director of any Gibraltar company.
